finalText:
## What happened

Single root cause: **Redis went away and never came back, and the service had no backpressure to survive it.** Full cascade in ~17m45s.

**Timeline** (all `logs/app.log`, times UTC):

| Time | Line | Event |
|---|---|---|
| 02:00:00 – 02:14:03 | 1–181 | Healthy. 170 requests, all 200, avg 76ms, cache hit ratio 0.90–0.95. Zero WARN/ERROR. |
| **02:14:07.113** | `app.log:182` | `redis connection lost: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.12:6379` — the trigger |
| 02:14:07.114 | `app.log:183` | `cache layer degraded — falling back to direct store reads` |
| 02:14:08 → | `app.log:184`+ | Cache miss storm (174 events) — every read now hits the backing store |
| 02:14:10 → | `app.log:185`+ | `TimeoutError: request timed out after 5000ms (store overloaded)` — 173 occurrences |
| 02:14:12 → | `app.log:186`+ | Queue depth climbing, starts at 52 |
| 02:15:26 – 02:31:26 | 13 lines | `redis reconnect attempt 0…12 failed` — all ECONNREFUSED, ~80s apart, never succeeds |
| **02:29:12** | `app.log:647` | Queue depth **502 > max 500** — limit breached, but nothing sheds load; it keeps growing to 568 |
| 02:31:44.902 | `app.log:717` | `JavaScript heap out of memory (request backlog)` on worker-2 |
| 02:31:45.001 | `app.log:718` | `FATAL [supervisor] worker-2 exited with code 134, restarting` |
| **02:31:52.318** | `app.log:719` | `FATAL [supervisor] api unresponsive, killing process group — service down` |

## The causal chain

Redis at `10.0.0.12:6379` refused connections → cache fell back to direct store reads → 100% miss rate overloaded the backing store → 5s timeouts on every request → requests piled into the queue at a steady ~3/sec with no ceiling enforcement → queue blew past its 500 cap at 02:29:12 → the backlog exhausted the heap 2.5 min later → worker OOM'd (exit 134 = SIGABRT), supervisor killed the whole process group.

## Two things that turned an outage into a total failure

1. **The `max 500` queue limit is logged but not enforced.** Depth 502→568 with no rejection, no 503s, no shedding. That cap is decorative. Enforcing it would have kept the process alive and degraded to partial failure instead of full death.
2. **Reconnect never gave up or opened a circuit.** 13 attempts at a flat ~80s interval, all ECONNREFUSED. Meanwhile every request kept optimistically going the slow path. A circuit breaker after 2–3 failures would have let you fail fast instead of accumulating a 5-second-timeout backlog.

Redis being down is the incident; both of the above are why it took the service with it. Root cause for *why* Redis refused connections isn't in this log — ECONNREFUSED means the port was closed, so check Redis-side logs / whether that host was restarted or evicted at 02:14.

## Two caveats

- **The log is dated 2026-07-04, not last night (2026-08-26).** This is ~7 weeks old. Either it's a stale/archived file or rotation isn't working and you're looking at the wrong incident. Worth confirming before you act on it.
- The log ends at the `service down` line — there's no recovery evidence here, so I can't tell you how it came back.
